title: AI, Machine Learning, Deep Learning and Transformers
tagline: From first Python script to building a mini GPT and fine-tuning LLMs.
summary: In 20 weeks (5 months), students go from writing their first Python script to training neural networks, building a small GPT from scratch and fine-tuning modern Transformer models. Every week ends with a project on GitHub, and key algorithms are built from scratch once before students use libraries, so nothing is a black box.
prerequisites: None. No prior Python or ML required; Class 12 maths is enough, and ML maths is taught in Week 5.
audience: Undergraduate students from any branch. No prior Python or ML required. Class 12 maths is enough; ML maths is taught in Week 5.
format: Two 90-minute theory + live-coding sessions and one 3-hour lab each week (about 6 contact hours), plus 3-4 hours of self-study and project work.
teamSize: Weekly projects are individual; the Week 8 competition and the capstone are in teams of 2-4.
hardware: Any laptop with 8 GB RAM. GPU work runs on free Google Colab / Kaggle notebooks.
outcome: A portfolio of 19 projects on GitHub / Hugging Face Hub and one deployed capstone model with a demo video.
learningOutcomes: Write clean Python and use NumPy, Pandas and Matplotlib to clean, explore and visualise data.
Explain the linear algebra, calculus and probability behind ML, and implement gradient descent from scratch.
Build, tune, evaluate and explain classical ML models with scikit-learn (regression, classification, ensembles, clustering, PCA).
Build neural networks from scratch and in PyTorch, including CNNs for images and RNNs / LSTMs for sequences.
Explain attention and the Transformer architecture, and build a small GPT from scratch.
Use and fine-tune pretrained Transformers (BERT, ViT, small LLMs) with Hugging Face, including LoRA / QLoRA.
Track experiments, deploy models as apps or APIs, and check models for bias, errors and failure cases.
highlights: No prior Python or ML needed - Class 12 maths is enough
Key algorithms built from scratch before using libraries
Build a mini GPT and fine-tune small LLMs with QLoRA
19 portfolio projects plus a deployed team capstone

phases.title: Python and data foundations
phases.summary: Most of an ML engineer's time goes into data. This phase builds fluent Python, fast array programming with NumPy, and the Pandas and plotting skills needed to clean and explore real datasets.
phases.gate: Load a messy real dataset, clean it, and explain it with clear charts and written insights.

phases.title: Maths for ML and classical ML
phases.summary: Students learn the maths behind learning, implement key algorithms from scratch, then master scikit-learn: regression, classification, ensembles, clustering and deployment, which still solve most real-world tabular problems.
phases.gate: Take a tabular problem from raw data to a tuned, explained and deployed ML model.

phases.title: Deep learning with PyTorch
phases.summary: Students build a neural network by hand, then use PyTorch on free GPUs to train CNNs for images and RNNs / LSTMs for sequences, with good training practice and experiment tracking.
phases.gate: Train, debug and deploy a PyTorch image or text model, and explain backpropagation.

phases.title: Transformers, LLMs and capstone
phases.summary: Students build attention and a mini GPT from scratch, fine-tune pretrained Transformers with Hugging Face, fine-tune a small LLM with LoRA, and finish with MLOps, responsible AI and capstone demo day.
phases.gate: Explain and implement attention, fine-tune a pretrained Transformer, and ship a capstone.

weeks.title: Python basics
outcomes: Set up Python, Jupyter, Colab and Git.
Write programs with variables, conditionals, loops and functions.
Use AI coding assistants while understanding every line.
topics: Course intro: what AI, ML, DL and Transformers are, with live demos
Installing Python 3.12+, VS Code, Jupyter; using Google Colab
Variables, data types, operators, strings and f-strings
weeks.lab: Pair-program a number-guessing game, then refactor it into functions. Push to GitHub.

project.title: Student report-card generator
project.brief: Reads marks for a class, calculates totals, percentages, grades and rank, and prints formatted report cards.
deliverables: At least 4 functions with clear names
Class topper and subject averages shown
project.stretch: Export report cards to a text file per student.

weeks.title: Data structures, files, OOP and Git
outcomes: Choose the right data structure for a problem.
Read and write CSV and JSON files.
Model problems with classes and dataclasses.
topics: Modules and packages; pip and virtual environments
weeks.lab: Build a contact book with add / search / delete saved to JSON.

project.title: Personal expense tracker
project.brief: A class-based app to add, filter and summarise expenses by category and month, stored in CSV.
deliverables: Expense modelled as a class or dataclass
project.stretch: Add a monthly bar chart (preview of Week 4).

weeks.title: NumPy and vectorised thinking
outcomes: Create and manipulate arrays of any shape.
Replace Python loops with fast vectorised operations.
Treat images and datasets as arrays.
topics: Images as 3D arrays (height x width x channels)
weeks.lab: Speed challenge: rewrite five loop-based functions in NumPy and measure the speed-up.

project.title: Image filters with NumPy
project.brief: Load a photo as an array and implement filters without image libraries.
deliverables: Grayscale, flip, crop, brightness and blur
Timing comparison vs a loop version
project.stretch: Implement edge detection with a Sobel filter (preview of convolutions).

weeks.title: Pandas, cleaning, visualisation and EDA
outcomes: Load, clean and reshape real-world data with Pandas.
Choose the right chart for a question.
Run an exploratory data analysis and communicate insights.
topics: Series and DataFrames; loading CSV / Excel
Selecting, filtering, sorting, groupby, merge, pivot
Cleaning: missing values, duplicates, types, outliers
Matplotlib and Seaborn: histograms, box, scatter, line, heatmaps
weeks.lab: Clean a deliberately messy dataset and produce 5 charts that answer given questions.

project.title: EDA report on a real dataset (Phase 1 project)
project.brief: Pick an Indian open dataset (IPL, air quality, crop production, census, etc.) and produce an EDA notebook.
deliverables: 10 written insights backed by the data

weeks.title: Maths for ML (taught with code)
outcomes: Use vectors and matrices to represent data and models.
Compute gradients and explain gradient descent.
Reason with probability and basic statistics.
topics: Vectors, dot products, norms; matrices as transformations
Derivatives, partial derivatives, gradients, chain rule
Gradient descent: learning rate, convergence, local minima
Probability: distributions, expectation, variance, Bayes' rule
weeks.lab: Implement numerical gradients and compare with hand-derived ones.

project.title: Gradient descent visualiser + probability simulations
project.brief: Animate gradient descent on 2D functions and run Monte Carlo simulations.
deliverables: Monte Carlo for at least 3 problems (e.g. birthday problem)
Short write-up of what was learned

weeks.title: ML fundamentals and linear regression
outcomes: Explain supervised learning, training and generalisation.
Implement linear regression from scratch and with scikit-learn.
Diagnose overfitting and apply regularisation.
topics: What ML is; supervised vs unsupervised; features and labels
Linear regression from scratch with gradient descent
Metrics: MAE, RMSE, R^2; polynomial features; Ridge and Lasso
weeks.lab: Fit models of increasing complexity and plot training vs validation error.

project.title: House price predictor
project.brief: Predict house prices with a from-scratch model and scikit-learn, and compare.
deliverables: From-scratch and scikit-learn versions agree closely
project.stretch: Add regularisation and tune its strength.

weeks.title: Classification
outcomes: Train and compare common classifiers.
Pick evaluation metrics that match the problem.
Turn text into features.
topics: Confusion matrix, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC
Choosing metrics when classes are imbalanced
weeks.lab: Build a decision tree by hand on a tiny dataset, then check with scikit-learn.

project.title: SMS spam or placement predictor
project.brief: Train at least 3 classifiers, compare them, and analyse the mistakes.
deliverables: 3+ models compared on the same split
Confusion matrix and 10 misclassified examples discussed
project.stretch: Try a simple threshold tuning to trade precision for recall.

weeks.title: Ensembles, feature engineering and tuning
outcomes: Use random forests and gradient boosting.
Engineer useful features and build pipelines.
Tune hyperparameters with cross-validation.
topics: Feature engineering: encoding, scaling, dates, interactions
weeks.lab: Competition kick-off: teams explore the data and submit a baseline.

project.title: In-class Kaggle-style competition (teams)
project.brief: Teams compete on a private leaderboard (e.g. loan default prediction).
deliverables: Short write-up: what worked and what did not

weeks.title: Unsupervised learning
outcomes: Group data with clustering algorithms.
Reduce dimensions for modelling and visualisation.
Detect unusual data points.
topics: PCA: intuition and maths link to Week 5
weeks.lab: Compress images with PCA and see how many components are needed.

project.title: Customer segmentation
project.brief: Cluster retail customers and describe each segment.
project.stretch: Flag unusual customers with anomaly detection.

weeks.title: ML in practice and deployment
outcomes: Avoid common real-world ML mistakes.
Explain individual predictions.
Deploy a model as an app or API.
topics: Data leakage and how to spot it
Quick UIs with Streamlit / Gradio; Hugging Face Spaces
weeks.lab: Find the leakage in three deliberately broken notebooks.

project.title: End-to-end deployed ML app (Phase 2 project)
project.brief: From raw data to a deployed app (e.g. crop recommendation, loan approval, student dropout risk).
deliverables: Clean pipeline from raw data to model
SHAP explanation shown for each prediction
Model card with limits and fairness notes
project.stretch: Add input validation and logging to the API.

weeks.title: Neural networks from scratch
outcomes: Explain neurons, layers and activation functions.
Derive and implement backpropagation.
Train a network with mini-batch SGD.
topics: Layers, activations: sigmoid, tanh, ReLU, softmax
Backpropagation with the chain rule, step by step
Weight initialisation; debugging with gradient checks
weeks.lab: Hand-compute one backprop step on paper, then verify in code.

project.title: NumPy neural network on MNIST
project.brief: A 2-layer network in pure NumPy that recognises handwritten digits.
project.stretch: Add a third layer and momentum.

weeks.title: PyTorch fundamentals
outcomes: Use tensors and autograd.
Write a clean, reusable training loop.
Train on a GPU.
topics: Saving and loading checkpoints; Colab / Kaggle GPUs
weeks.lab: Port the Week 11 network to PyTorch and confirm it matches.

project.title: Fashion-MNIST classifier
project.brief: Train and improve an MLP in PyTorch.

weeks.title: CNNs and transfer learning
outcomes: Explain convolutions and pooling.
Fine-tune pretrained vision models.
Interpret what a CNN has learned.
topics: Intro to object detection (YOLO) and segmentation
weeks.lab: Build a small CNN on CIFAR-10, then beat it with a pretrained model.

project.title: Plant disease or Indian food classifier
project.brief: Fine-tune a pretrained CNN on a real image dataset.
deliverables: Train / validation / test split without leakage
Grad-CAM for correct and wrong predictions
project.stretch: Run YOLO on campus photos and count objects.

weeks.title: Sequence models
outcomes: Represent words as vectors.
Build RNN / LSTM models for text.
Explain why RNNs led to attention.
topics: Simple time-series forecasting; limits of RNNs
weeks.lab: Explore word-embedding analogies (king - man + woman).

project.title: Review sentiment analyser
project.brief: An LSTM classifier for movie or product reviews (English or a regional language).
deliverables: LSTM beats or matches the Week 7 TF-IDF baseline
Demo that scores any typed review

weeks.title: Training deep models well
outcomes: Prevent and diagnose overfitting.
Track and compare experiments.
Explain the main generative model families.
topics: Dropout, weight decay, batch norm, early stopping
Weights & Biases or MLflow experiment tracking
weeks.lab: Train an autoencoder to denoise images.

project.title: Deployed deep learning app (Phase 3 project)
project.brief: Train a vision or text model with tracked experiments and deploy it on Hugging Face Spaces.
project.stretch: Export the model to ONNX and compare speed.

weeks.title: Attention and the Transformer
outcomes: Explain self-attention with queries, keys and values.
Implement a Transformer block.
Compare encoder, decoder and encoder-decoder models.
topics: Scaled dot-product attention, step by step
Encoder vs decoder (BERT vs GPT vs T5)
Reading 'Attention Is All You Need' together
weeks.lab: Compute attention by hand for a 3-word sentence, then in code.

project.title: Transformer block from scratch
project.brief: Implement attention and a full Transformer block in PyTorch.
project.stretch: Train the block on a toy sequence-reversal task.

weeks.title: Tokenisation and building a mini GPT
outcomes: Explain subword tokenisation.
Train a decoder-only Transformer.
Control text generation with sampling settings.
topics: Building and training a mini GPT
Scaling laws and what changes at large scale
weeks.lab: Train a BPE tokenizer on a local-language corpus and inspect the tokens.

project.title: Mini GPT
project.brief: Train a small GPT on a text corpus (e.g. Thirukkural, Tamil / Hindi news, Shakespeare) and generate text.
deliverables: Model and training loop written by the student
Parameter count and training time reported

weeks.title: Hugging Face and fine-tuning pretrained models
outcomes: Use pretrained models from the Hugging Face Hub.
Fine-tune Transformers for classification and NER.
Build semantic search with sentence embeddings.
topics: Pretrained BERT, T5 and Vision Transformer (ViT)

project.title: Fine-tuned BERT model

weeks.title: Large language models

project.title: LoRA fine-tuned domain assistant (Phase 4 project)
project.brief: Fine-tune a small open LLM (1-3B) on a domain dataset (e.g. college FAQs) and compare approaches.
deliverables: QLoRA fine-tune completed on free GPU
Fine-tuned vs prompting vs RAG compared on 30 questions

weeks.title: MLOps, responsible AI and demo day
outcomes: Serve and monitor models in production.
Audit a model for bias and misuse.
Present an ML product to a panel.
topics: Responsible AI: bias audits, privacy, explainability
Portfolio building; careers in ML engineering and research
Demo day: teams present their deployed capstone model to a panel (10-minute live demo + 5-minute Q&A; evaluation and bias report; public app, GitHub repo, model card and demo video)
weeks.lab: Final dry runs, then demo day.

capstone.summary: Teams of 2-4 train or fine-tune a model and deploy it to solve a real problem. The capstone is worth 35% of the final grade and is the centrepiece of each student's portfolio. Minimum requirements: a real dataset (public or collected) with its source and licence documented; a simple baseline and at least one deep learning or Transformer model that beats it; tracked experiments (W&B or MLflow) with a clear evaluation metric; error analysis and a basic bias / fairness check; and a deployed app or API, a GitHub repo with README, a model card and a demo video. Teams may propose their own idea if it meets the minimum requirements.
ideas: Crop disease detector: identifies plant diseases from leaf photos and suggests actions (CNNs, transfer learning, mobile-friendly app)
Regional-language news classifier: classifies Tamil / Hindi news by topic and flags fake-news signals (multilingual Transformers, fine-tuning)
Regional speech-to-text: fine-tunes a speech model (e.g. Whisper) on local accents (audio models, fine-tuning, WER)
Traffic and helmet detection: counts vehicles and detects helmet violations from road video (object detection (YOLO), video)
Resume-job matcher with bias audit: ranks resumes against job descriptions and audits for bias (embeddings, ranking, fairness)
Domain assistant with LoRA: a fine-tuned small LLM for college, legal-aid or agriculture FAQs (QLoRA, RAG, LLM evaluation)
Sign-language recognition: recognises hand signs from webcam video (CNN / LSTM or Transformer, pose estimation)
Medical image classifier (research demo): classifies chest X-rays, clearly labelled as not for diagnosis (CNNs, Grad-CAM, responsible AI)

milestones.item: Proposal: problem, users, dataset source and licence, baseline approach, success metric. Instructor approval required.
Data and baseline: cleaned dataset, EDA, and a simple baseline model with its score.
Model v1: deep learning or Transformer model beating the baseline; experiments tracked.
Mid-review: 10-minute review with a TA covering results so far, error analysis and plan for final week.
Deployed: public app or API, evaluation report, error and bias analysis.
Demo day: 10-minute live demo + 5-minute Q&A; final repo, model card, demo video (<= 5 min).

assessment.component: Weekly projects (15 non-phase weeks, about 1.7% each)
Phase projects (Weeks 4, 10, 15 and 19, 7.5% each, with a 5-minute live demo)
Concept quizzes (one 20-minute quiz per phase, 4 total)
Capstone (proposal 5%, final model and deployment 15%, evaluation and bias report 5%, demo day presentation 10%)

policies: AI coding tools are allowed, except on from-scratch assignments (Weeks 5, 6, 11, 16 and 17), which students must write and explain themselves. Demos include questions on code and maths.
Academic integrity: sharing ideas is fine; copying another student's repository is not. Cite any code, tutorial or template used.
Data ethics: use datasets you have the right to use, document their licences, and never upload personal data without consent.
Late work: 10% penalty per day, up to 3 days. Phase projects and demo day cannot be submitted late without prior approval.
Attendance: at least 80% of labs required to be eligible for the capstone.
Responsible use: models must not be presented as medical, legal or financial advice; demos in sensitive areas must be clearly labelled as research prototypes.
